artifacts.notes: Exact HTML response acquired and inspected. It identifies 4Q560 and presents six lines assigned to fragment 1 and seven lines assigned to fragment 2, with lacunae and uncertainty visible.

edition.notes: CAL states that its text is based on photograph PAM 43.602, with some readings from Joseph Naveh, Israel Exploration Journal 48 (1998), pp. 252–261, especially p. 256, and Émile Puech's editio princeps in DJD 37, pp. 291ff. The dated delivery controls CAL's fragmentary Aramaic transcription, not the photograph, full DJD apparatus, an English translation, or independent adjudication of readings.
edition.publication: Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon, Hebrew Union College, public web text acquired 2026-07-27
edition.title: 4Q560 (Aramaic Magic Book)

passages.context: The entire CAL delivery was inspected. It preserves two short, heavily lacunose fragment sequences: the first contains harmful-being and bodily-affliction vocabulary, while the second preserves spirit and adjuratory language. This verifies CAL's fragment architecture and readable lexical categories, not a continuous reconstruction, translation, manuscript-image collation, complete formula, intended use, community ownership, date, efficacy, ordinary practice, diagnosis, Jewish or Christian authorship, influence, continuity, equivalence with Christian exorcism, or operational instruction.
passages.notes: No formula or procedure is transcribed. The fragmentary state prevents recovery of a complete sequence from this exact witness.

work.description: A very fragmentary Aramaic Cave 4 text conventionally described as a magic book or incantation text. Edition records must preserve lacunae, uncertain readings, fragment arrangement, and the distinction between transcription, reconstruction, translation, and interpretation.
